about: SL8's restated prompt table for story-faceless-long. Each row restates one prompt recorded in the capability assessment (the Higgsfield faceless-video skill and its style, script and delivery references, captured 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-26) in SL8 words, keeps its structure and instructions, and cites it by research id in `from`. Nothing is copied: the source states no licence. The wording was written for the vendor's own engines and has not been run on the fal models this skill defaults to. Placeholders are {CAPITALS}; fill them, never send a brace.

rows.use: step 7: the style key (index 0)
rows.prompt: A tidy {STYLE} look sample: a single easy-to-read subject, such as a small friendly object or a tiny scene, drawn in this look so that its linework, shading and colors are obvious at first sight. Pleasant, balanced and clear. Do not draw color swatches, palette bars, chips or squares, captions, letters, labels, a watermark or anything laid out like a reference sheet.

rows.use: step 7: the same sample when the key is built from the house formula alone
rows.prompt: Render a {STYLE} look sample as an attractive, legible vignette (one recognizable small subject or a little scene) rather than shapeless blobs, so the stroke weight, the shading and the colors can be judged at a glance. Leave out swatch strips, colour squares, chips, labels, any text, a watermark and any sheet-like layout. It is a look anchor, never a final frame.

rows.use: step 14: every Fairy Tale & Myth / Cinematic Storybook block, plus its constraints
rows.prompt: Put in every block: CLASSIC HAND-DRAWN 2D ANIMATION, drawn ON TWOS (about twelve drawings a second), with deliberately stepped pose-to-pose movement and tiny holds between poses, snappy key poses, NOT smooth, NOT fluid in-betweening, NOT slow motion; slow, graceful, dreamy camera moves are welcome. Add to CONSTRAINTS: smooth or fluid motion, slow motion, motion blur, a sixty-frames look. Keep the 3D-render ban, because this look is 2D.

rows.use: steps 14 and 17: moderation-safe staging for Storybook
rows.prompt: Grim images of death trip the video model's safety filter even in a painted fairy tale. Leave out cloaked boatmen and hooded figures, spirits of the dead, bodies, rivers of the dead, close menacing claw shadows and anything that reads as harm to a person. Carry a dark or underworld mood with buildings, light and landscape instead: gates, torchlight, fog, pale flowers, ruins, moonlight. Characters stay plainly adult and the usual child-safety rules hold. If a dark beat keeps failing, restage it as an empty, atmospheric place.

rows.use: step 23: the music bed prompt
rows.prompt: Turn the topic's mood into tempo, instruments and feel, in one sentence (two at most), instrumental with no singing and no lyrics. Calm or cosy topics: mellow lo-fi or warm marimba over airy pads at an easy middle tempo. Adventure or action: a brighter, bouncy small-band groove. Acoustic, jazz, lo-fi and small-combo wording tends to clear moderation; keep away from grand orchestral writing and from EDM or bass-drop terms, which are known to trip content filters. Download it and pass it to the assembler as --music.

rows.use: step 23: the bed prompt for Fairy Tale & Myth / Cinematic Storybook
rows.prompt: The mood is dark and enchanted ambience: mysterious, calm, hushed and dreamlike, with long soft strings, a distant harp, a faint music box, a low choir pad and a far bell; instrumental, with no drums and no singing. It sits under the voice at --music-vol 0.09 with the duck, and is never bright or bouncy. A customer's own file always wins; if generation fails, ship without a bed and say so.

rows.use: step 19: the text sent to the voice model: the plain spoken words (a direction wrapper only for a route that documents tags)
rows.prompt:
{SPOKEN WORDS}
Default for fal-ai/elevenlabs/tts/multilingual-v2: send the line exactly as the manifest keeps it. That model has no direction or audio-tag syntax, so a bracketed delivery phrase, a timecode or a sound word would be read aloud. Delivery comes from word choice, the voice preset, `stability` and `style`, and `previous_text`/`next_text`. Only for a route whose facts row documents tags (eleven-v3 is silent on them, so name the route in a Known result first): [{DELIVERY}, {OPTIONAL BLOCK MOOD}, begins talking at once] {SPOKEN WORDS}.

rows.prompt: [a small scoff] [a dry chuckle] [a sigh] [a soft laugh] [a mock gasp] [a whisper]

rows.use: steps 10 and 19: Kids lines
rows.prompt: Kids lines take 17 to 21 words in each 10 s block, in the same voice but quicker and more excited. The excitement lives in the words themselves: short springy phrases, sound words and catch phrases written as spoken words ("Oh wow!", "Whoa!"), which count in the budget. On multilingual-v2 no bracket is sent (it has no tag syntax); a route that documents tags may take a {DELIVERY} phrase that names the feeling plainly, for example: thrilled, smiling storyteller, quick springy pace, bright happy tone, bubbling with delight.

rows.use: steps 10, 11 and 14: Kids narration and staging
rows.prompt: On screen the characters respond to the narrator: when the voice greets or asks something, that block's shot shows the reaction (a turn to camera and a wave, a nod, a gasp, a clap, a point, a finger to the lips), written into the shot and timed to the line. Mouths never move with the words; reacting is not talking. The narrator speaks both to the characters and to the viewer, and on lines aimed at the viewer the characters look straight into the lens. A question closes its block's line; the cut between blocks is the beat where the viewer answers, and the following block starts by giving the answer. Never leave a long gap inside a line for an answer.

rows.use: step 10: before the script is locked
rows.prompt: 1. Would the hook land with no context at all? 2. Can every number and date be traced to the research? 3. Does each block carry one idea, with every cut serving it? 4. Would shuffling the build blocks break the story (so they escalate)? 5. Is the turn a surprise and not a recap? 6. Does the closing line echo the hook and settle the through-line? 7. Is every full-block line 20 to 23 words (Kids 17 to 21), smooth, light on commas, paced for a full block, with humor that suits the channel? 8. In each block, does the shot text put the concrete things and amounts its own line names on screen, with no action motif twice in a row or over its budget?

rows.use: step 4: the eight intake fields
rows.prompt: Before any call other than intake, all eight fields must be set: channel type, style, topic, length, aspect, subtitles on or off, cover yes or no, and the one locked voice. On this machine a field the brief leaves out takes its stated default and the delivery says so; nothing is asked.

rows.use:
step 11: work/

/script_manifest.json
rows.prompt: Top-level fields: the topic; the genre; animation_mode set to fully_animated; channel_type; the style key name; an assets roster (id, kind, name); through_line, giving its name, its asset, how it progresses and how it resolves; arc, giving the hook, the list of build beats, the turn and the payoff; blocks, where each holds its number n, arc_role, the spoken vo_line, its location, through_line_state, the shots list and assets_used; and sources as full research links. Genre follows the channel by a fixed map: an Explainer is education, a History video is history, Kids is kids and Fairy Tale & Myth is storytelling; never the display name. The through-line asset sits in every block's assets_used.

rows.use: step 13: Kids Talking Characters fields
rows.prompt: Set talking_characters true at the top of the manifest and alternate block_kind between narration and dialogue, beginning with narration. Narration blocks keep 17 to 21 words. A dialogue block holds 16 to 22 words in all, spoken by one or two named characters, and its voice comes from the clip's own sound instead of a narrator take. The flag is never set in song mode.

rows.use: step 13: a dialogue block's vo_line and speakers
rows.prompt: In a dialogue block the vo_line field holds everything said in the order it is heard, and speakers lists the one or two speakers in that order; keep who says which line in the written script. The validator checks the flag, the alternation, the word bands and the number of speakers.

prompt (style): "{A|A dance-along} children's song, sung by a {gentle|cheerful, lively} female singer whose voice smiles; a true tune with verses and a returning chorus, not narration; a steady constant beat at {100|112} BPM in plain 4/4 with no tempo changes, no slowing and no gaps between sections; eight-syllable lines in trochaic stress, sung one syllable per beat, each line starting on beat one as one 4-bar phrase; the chorus repeats verbatim; a {sweet|bouncy} nursery melody in {C|G} major moving in small steps inside one octave, verses lower and playful, the chorus a touch higher and brighter; {INSTRUMENT SET}; a clean, warm mix with the voice up front; {soft and tuneful|lively but sweet}, perfectly in tune and suited to toddlers."

DANCE-ALONG, for parties, exercise and action: G major at 112 BPM, a clap every other beat, a springy picked ukulele with the bass tied to the kick drum, marimba and sparkly bells, and a chorus full of action words such as clap, stomp, jump and spin.

rows.use: step 14: how Stickman is named in every prompt
rows.prompt: a rough paint-program web comic look: thin shaky black lines, flat solid fills, stick figures with egg heads and dot eyes, plain single-color backdrops

extremely minimal flat 2D web comic drawing: thin outlines of one even weight in black, egg-shaped heads with small dot eyes and a single stroke for a mouth, simple noodle arms and legs, flat solid color inside the lines, with NO shading, NO gradients and NO texture, a deadpan bare-bones design and plain backdrops of one flat color.
Watercolor Chronicle: loose painted watercolor washes over fine ink sketching, a quiet period palette and soft paper grain; a storybook way to tell a documentary.

documentary illustration in hand-painted watercolor and ink: free, expressive washes laid over fine, assured ink drawing that shows each pen stroke, a quiet, restrained period palette leaning warm toward sepia, soft cotton-paper texture where washes bleed at their edges, sketchy unfinished margins that fade into bare paper at the frame edge, costume and architecture true to the period, painterly light from one side with soft shadows, a faint paper grain, and gentle painterly movement in which washes seem to breathe and lines feel alive, never mechanical; illustrated, not photographic, never live action.
soft painterly movement, with breathing washes, living lines and a slight parallax between the painted layers
the quiet period watercolor colors of the references, warm toward sepia; no bright modern hues, no neon and no gradients apart from the washes

Studio 3D preschool look: chunky, rounded cartoon characters in 3D with a soft shiny toy finish, big lovable googly eyes and small friendly smiles, smooth surfaces between matte clay and glossy plastic with no hard edges, clear and readable outlines, bright, saturated candy colors such as red, yellow, blue, orange and green, soft gentle studio light with rounded soft shadows, a clean seamless pure white backdrop with plenty of empty space, a cheerful preschool CGI feel; not photographic, not live action, and no writing on screen.

{MOTION} (dimensional): bouncy, springy, friendly movement with hops, wobbles and blinks, and smooth, gentle camera moves; remove the 3D-render ban from CONSTRAINTS. PALETTE LOCK: the bright candy colors of the references on a seamless pure white backdrop; add no color and no gradient behind.

soft pastel preschool cartoon in flat 2D vector: a palette of soft pink, pale baby blue, mint, sandy yellow and lavender, every outline tinted one step darker than its fill and never black, big round eyes with white around large black pupils and tiny white highlights, simple rounded forms with natural curves, cel shading in clear flat shadow shapes, warm friendly faces, uncluttered backdrops shaded by a gentle, soft gradient, and nothing with sharp corners and no texture.

{MOTION} (flat): simple, limited animation held on twos with soft bouncy easing; keep the 3D-render ban in CONSTRAINTS. PALETTE LOCK: the reference pastels (pink, a pale baby blue, mint, a sandy yellow and lavender), nothing new, outlines one shade darker and never black.

bright stylized 3D cartoon: characters built round and chunky on purpose, with huge sparkling eyes full of feeling, broad warm grins and readable outlines, clean glossy toy-like surfaces, soft studio light with almost no shadow, glossy cartoon CGI and never photographic, an EXTREMELY VIVID candy palette pushed loud and punchy (cherry red, a sunny yellow, sky blue, orange and lime, all at full strength, never muted and never pastel), cosy storybook places made of soft, rounded shapes beneath a bright blue sky dotted with puffy clouds, a safe and cheerful mood where there is adventure yet never real danger, and lively, springy comic touches such as sweat drops, surprise marks and whoosh lines.

{MOTION} (dimensional): lively, springy movement with comic accents and an energetic yet gentle camera that pushes in, orbits and cranes back; remove the 3D-render ban. PALETTE LOCK: the vivid, saturated candy primaries of the references, turned up bold; no drift toward muted or pastel and no new color; if heroes recur through the script, each one keeps its own single signature color.

thin-line illustration drawn by hand in ink: even, thin, slightly shaky black outlines on a PURE WHITE ground, figures and objects left without color, simple round-bodied figures with dots for eyes, tiny stroke mouths and wildly expressive eyebrows, soft, flat pale-grey shadow shapes beneath things, soft-edged and never hatched, all flat 2D with no gradients and no texture, STRICTLY NEUTRAL GREYSCALE with no color cast and no blue or cool tint and no tones except pure white, a neutral grey and black, quiet deadpan humor, tidy disciplined lines, never photographic.
{MOTION} (flat): simple, limited animation held on twos; keep the 3D-render ban. PALETTE LOCK: only pure white, a neutral grey and black; any color counts as a fault.

cheerful, minimal poster cartoon in flat 2D vector: bold rounded geometric shapes without outlines, flat solid fills, NO gradients and NO texture, friendly round blobs for characters with little curved shut eyes or plain dot eyes and a small, simple smile, one quiet flat offset shadow in a darker tone per shape, a vivid, saturated set of colors (tangerine, sunny yellow, cobalt, bubblegum pink, grass green and deep navy) with touches of black and white, one plain flat backdrop color, and, as its trademark, a little white sparkle diamond.
